framing: A theorem eliminates candidates, not open problems: a candidate is a proposed answer or design that commits to quantities the theorem forbids. Three states: eliminated (the violated relation with the numbers, kernel-checked where marked), consistent (not ruled out by these theorems; never "feasible"), cannot-rule (a required input or assumption is missing). An elimination holds only under the law's own assumptions, listed per constraint; three of the four original statements were judged narrower in scope than their claims by the assessor, and a candidate eliminated by a narrower statement is eliminated only under that statement's assumptions.
nextConstraint: Strength scaling as L^2 (cross-section), which with the cube law would turn Galileo's square-cube argument into an elimination; not formalised.

neutral_substitution_rate.unit: substitutions per site per generation, neutral sites

gene_copies_M.unit: gene copies in the population (2N for diploids)

fixation_probability.unit: probability that one new mutant copy is eventually fixed

selection_coefficient_nonnegative.unit: commitment that selection does not oppose the mutant (s >= 0)

expected_substitutions_total.unit: expected substitutions over sites_G sites and generations_T generations

mean_fitness_change.unit: change in mean fitness over one round of selection

asexual_fraction_initial.unit: fraction of females that are asexual, now (0 < q < 1)

asexual_fraction_after.unit: fraction of females that are asexual after generations_n

length_ratio.unit: L2 / L1, the same linear dimension of the same body family

loglog_exponent.unit: d log W / d log L between the two sizes

blueprint_file.unit: path to an emitted blueprint JSON (organism-design/examples/*.json)

mutation_rate_ratio.unit: ratio of the mutation rates of two neutral lineages (lineage 2 over lineage 1)

neutral_substitution_rate_ratio.unit: ratio of the neutral substitution rates of the same two lineages

mean_fitness_change_sign.unit: sign of the change in mean fitness over one round of selection: positive, zero or negative

asexual_odds_growth_factor.unit: factor by which the odds of asexual females grow per generation

assumptions.neutral_wright_fisher: strictly neutral mutations, constant population size, Wright-Fisher reproduction, independent mutant fates (lean/Delphi/Kimura.lean header)
assumptions.wright_fisher_selection: Wright-Fisher sampling with relative fitness 1+s for the mutant, s constant (lean/Delphi/Favored.lean header)
assumptions.independent_fates_definition: the expected count is Kimura's definition rate x generations: independent fates, constant M, mu and s, no linkage (lean/Delphi/Favored.lean header)
assumptions.fixed_fitnesses_one_locus: one haploid or clonal locus, fixed fitnesses within the step, infinite population, no mutation (lean/Delphi/Fisher.lean header)
assumptions.equal_fecundity_1to1: equal fecundity of sexual and asexual females, a 1:1 sex ratio, males contributing nothing, discrete generations (lean/Delphi/MaynardSmith.lean header)
assumptions.isometric_constant_density: the same body family scaled without change of shape or density, so W = k L^3 (lean/Delphi/Thompson.lean header)

constraints.property: the long-run rate at which neutral mutations become substitutions, relative to the mutation rate
constraints.rule: eliminated when the committed intervals for k and mu are disjoint; consistent when they overlap
constraints.canEliminate: only a candidate that commits to a neutral substitution rate different from its mutation rate (for example a neutral clock that scales with population size)
constraints.label: Neutral substitution rate equals the mutation rate

kernelChecked: A neutral absorbing chain on {0..M} copies (stochastic, mean-preserving, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state) fixes a mutant with probability i/M, with an explicit geometric error bound at every finite time t.
The Wright-Fisher binomial kernel is such a chain (row sums, mean preservation and absorption proved from Bernstein polynomial identities).
With u = 1/M the defined substitution rate M * mu * u equals mu, also in the diploid 2N form and as the t -> infinity limit.
assumed: Strict neutrality of the mutations.
Constant population size and Wright-Fisher reproduction (non-overlapping generations, multinomial sampling).

Independent fates of mutants: the substitution rate is DEFINED, as in Kimura 1968, as (new mutants per generation) x (fixation probability of one mutant). Interference between lineages is excluded by that definition, not proved absent.
The mutation rate mu per copy per generation is a free parameter; nothing here measures it.

assumptionsText: strictly neutral mutations, constant population size, Wright-Fisher reproduction, independent mutant fates (lean/Delphi/Kimura.lean header)

constraints.property: whether neutral substitution rates can differ between lineages that share a mutation rate (for example through population size)
constraints.rule: applies only when the committed mutation-rate ratio is exactly 1; then eliminated when the committed substitution-rate ratio is not 1
constraints.canEliminate: a candidate that attributes a difference in neutral substitution rate between lineages to anything other than a difference in mutation rate (population size, for instance)
constraints.label: Neutral substitution rate equals the mutation rate

constraints.property: the probability that a single new neutral mutant copy is eventually fixed
constraints.rule: eliminated when 1/M lies outside the committed interval for u
constraints.canEliminate: only a candidate that commits to a specific contradicting probability; it says nothing about which mutations arise or what they do
constraints.label: Kimura fixation probability of a mutant allele

kernelChecked: Fixation probability i/M for any neutral absorbing chain, hence for the exact finite Wright-Fisher chain (Delphi.NeutralChain.fixedBy_tendsto).
assumed: Neutral case only (s = 0). Kimura 1962 with selection in the diffusion limit is not formalised.

assumptionsText: strictly neutral mutations, constant population size, Wright-Fisher reproduction, independent mutant fates (lean/Delphi/Kimura.lean header)

constraints.property: the fixation probability of a single new mutant that selection does not oppose
constraints.rule: eliminated when the committed upper end of u is below 1/M
constraints.canEliminate: a candidate that says a neutral or favored mutant fixes less often than drift alone allows; it cannot eliminate on the high side (no upper bound in s is proved)
constraints.label: Fixation is at least i/M when selection does not oppose the mutant

kernelChecked: For any absorbing chain on {0..M} copies with E[X_{t+1} | X_t = i] >= i (stochastic, both ends absorbing, positive one-step escape from every interior state), P(fixed by t) is nondecreasing and bounded, its limit u(i) exists, and u(i) >= i/M (Delphi.FavoredChain.fixationProbability_ge); also u(i) <= 1.
Wright-Fisher sampling with success probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), s >= 0, is such a chain (Delphi.wrightFisherSelection), so a single new mutant fixes with probability at least 1/M.
The defined expected count M mu u T equals mu T for the neutral Wright-Fisher chain, is at least mu T for any favored chain, and is at most M mu T for any u <= 1.
assumed: The expected count is a DEFINITION (rate x generations, independent fates, Kimura 1968); linkage, interference, changing M, changing s and overlapping generations are excluded by it, not shown absent.
Selection enters only through the sampling probability (1+s) i / (M + s i), constant in time and across sites.
mu, T, M are free parameters; the module measures nothing. Which mutations are favored, how many a trait needs, and in what order, are outside it.

assumptionsText: Wright-Fisher sampling with relative fitness 1+s for the mutant, s constant (lean/Delphi/Favored.lean header)

constraints.property: the expected number of substitutions a lineage can accumulate over a given time
constraints.rule: eliminated when the committed lower end of E exceeds G * M * (upper end of mu) * T
constraints.canEliminate: a candidate that commits to an expected count above the mutation supply; a realised count, or a count without M, mu and T, cannot be ruled on
constraints.label: Fixation is at least i/M when selection does not oppose the mutant

constraints.property: the change in mean fitness over one round of selection, given the variance in fitness
constraints.rule: point commitments only: eliminated when delta_wbar * wbar != V exactly; interval commitments fall to C4b
constraints.canEliminate: a candidate that commits to all three quantities as exact values violating the identity
constraints.label: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)

kernelChecked: For one locus with finitely many types, frequencies p (nonneg, summing to 1), fixed fitnesses w and mean fitness > 0: selection p_next = p w / wbar yields wbar_next - wbar = Var(w)/wbar exactly.
Corollary: mean fitness never decreases under fixed fitnesses.
assumed: Haploid or clonal inheritance, so the variance in fitness IS the additive genetic variance; the diploid average-effect version is not formalised.
Fitnesses constant within the step (partial change): no dominance, epistasis, frequency dependence or environmental change.
Infinite population: deterministic frequencies, no drift, no mutation.

assumptionsText: one haploid or clonal locus, fixed fitnesses within the step, infinite population, no mutation (lean/Delphi/Fisher.lean header)

constraints.property: the sign of the change in mean fitness under fixed fitnesses
constraints.rule: eliminated when the committed upper end of delta_wbar is below 0
constraints.canEliminate: a candidate that says mean fitness falls under constant selection at one locus without mutation, drift, frequency dependence or environmental change

constraints.property: how fast an asexual lineage spreads among sexual females
constraints.rule: point commitments: eliminated when odds(q_n) != 2^n * odds(q_0) exactly on rationals
constraints.canEliminate: a candidate that commits to a spread faster or slower than the twofold doubling under the stated assumptions
constraints.label: Twofold cost of sex

kernelChecked: For 0 < q < 1 and fecundity f > 0 the odds of asexual to sexual females satisfy odds(q_next) = 2 odds(q), and f cancels.
Iterated n generations the odds are 2^n times the initial odds.
assumed: Anisogamy: males contribute nothing to offspring number or survival.
Equal fecundity and viability of sexual and asexual females and of their daughters.
Primary sex ratio exactly 1:1 in sexual broods; discrete non-overlapping generations; infinite population (deterministic fractions).

assumptionsText: equal fecundity of sexual and asexual females, a 1:1 sex ratio, males contributing nothing, discrete generations (lean/Delphi/MaynardSmith.lean header)

constraints.property: the per-generation growth factor of the odds of asexual females
constraints.rule: eliminated when the committed factor is not exactly 2
constraints.canEliminate: a candidate that commits to a per-generation odds factor other than 2 under the stated assumptions; a factor of 2 is the theorem and is consistent
constraints.label: Twofold cost of sex

constraints.property: the internal coherence of a proposed anatomical design: acyclic part_of, every term reaching the body root, no term excluded by taxon constraints

symbols.D: taxon statements pinned from Ubergraph for it

constraints.rule: consistent when the generated certificate compiles (kernel-evaluated checker); eliminated when the checker rejects the design, naming the failing condition (plain computation: the completeness direction check = false -> not well-formed is not proved)
constraints.canEliminate: a design whose part_of graph has a cycle or an orphan, or that keeps a term the pinned taxon statements exclude; it says nothing biological
constraints.kernelCheckable: on pass (certificate); on rejection the failing condition is reported by plain computation
constraints.label: An emitted anatomical blueprint graph is well-formed under its own rules

kernelChecked: Generic (any node type): edges strictly down in level ⟹ the part_of closure is transitive, strictly decreases the level, and is acyclic (Graph.acyclic_of_levelsDown, Graph.transGen_trans, Graph.transGen_level_lt).
Generic: edges closed and every non-root node has a whole ⟹ every node reaches the root (Graph.rooted_of, strong induction on level).
Generic: the Boolean checker is sound for LevelsDown, Closed, Acyclic, Rooted and the taxon conditions (wellFormed_of_check).

Per blueprint: the kernel evaluates the checker on the emitted graph and the pinned taxon rows (decide +kernel), and fixes the distinct-term counts per level and the graph size (lean/Delphi/Certificates/*.lean).
assumed: That Uberon and the Cell Ontology are correct and that Ubergraph served their part_of, subClassOf, never_in_taxon and in_taxon statements correctly and completely on the retrieval date: the graph and the taxon rows are data, pinned by hash and query.
That the five levels (body, organ system, organ, tissue, cell) are the right notion of depth; the theorems use only that edges strictly decrease it.
Nothing about any organism: not that it is real, that the anatomy is correct or complete, that any part was measured, or anything about a transition between forms.

constraints.property: how weight scales with a linear dimension under isometric scaling at constant density
constraints.rule: eliminated when the committed weight-ratio interval is disjoint from the cube of the length-ratio interval
constraints.canEliminate: the mass side of Galileo's square-cube argument only: a giant with unchanged proportions and density must weigh (L2/L1)^3 times more. Strength scaling as L^2 is NOT formalised, so a candidate claiming the giant can support itself is not ruled out by this theorem
constraints.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth

kernelChecked: If W L = k L^3 for all L > 0 with k > 0, then for L1 ≠ L2 the log-log slope (log W L2 − log W L1)/(log L2 − log L1) equals exactly 3 (cubeLaw_loglog_exponent) and W L2 / W L1 = (L2/L1)^3 (cubeLaw_ratio).
Contrapositive: two sizes with a log-log slope b ≠ 3 rule out W = k L^3 for every k (not_cubeLaw_of_exponent_ne_three).
assumed: A single linear dimension L and mass W of one body family; fixed shape and constant density are what W = k L^3 encodes.
Thompson's "mainly (though not wholly)" is not formalised: the theorem is exact, the law is approximate, and the tolerance band [2.5, 3.5] the claim test uses is a decision rule outside the module.
No data enters the module; the measured exponents are read from the claims thread's result files and pointed to.

assumptionsText: the same body family scaled without change of shape or density, so W = k L^3 (lean/Delphi/Thompson.lean header)

constraints.property: the log-log exponent of weight on a linear dimension under isometric scaling
constraints.rule: eliminated when the committed exponent interval excludes 3
constraints.canEliminate: a candidate that asserts isometry and a measured exponent whose interval excludes 3 (for example every NHANES window in the claims thread's test, if read as isometric)
constraints.label: Weight tends to vary as the cube of linear dimensions during growth
